Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.M.V.Maheshwarappa learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Mallikarjun Reddy.N.A. who represents Sri.Pradeep.B learned counsel for respondent No.1.
2.
The claimant is before this Court challenging the order that is passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bangalore in MVC No.2728/2020 dated 10.03.2023.
This appeal is filed seeking enhancement of compensation.

Submitting that the appellant has no grievance with regard to the notional income taken and the multiplier applied for calculating the loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability,
learned counsel Sri.M.V.Maheshwarappa submits that through the evidence of PW2 the appellant succeeded in establishing that the disability in respect of left lower limb is 36% and to the whole body is 12%.
However, the Tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 7% which is wholly unjustifiable.
Learned counsel also contends that the amount awarded under other heads is also grossly low.
4. Sri.Mallikarjun Reddy.
N.A. representing respondent No.1 on the other hand states that the Tribunal awarded a justifiable sum as compensation and therefore, the appeal is not maintainable.
Thanfi Kader.

sentences.text: As against the claim for Rs.10,00,000/-, the Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.5,08,018/- as compensation divided under following heads:
1 Pain
and sufferings

20,000-00 Loss of income during laid- 2 42,000-00 up period 3 Attendant charges, extra 23,400-00 NC: 2024:KHC:37447 nutritious food &
conveyance charges 4 Medical expenses 1,90,938-00 Loss of future income due 5 2,11,680-00 to disability Loss of future amenities & 6 20,000-00 happiness TOTAL 5,08,018-00 6.
It is not in dispute that the appellant sustained fracture of left tibia and he was treated with closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nail.
It is clearly brought on record that the implants were removed as the fracture was united.
Having considered this aspect and subjecting the evidence of PW2 to scrutiny, this Court is of the view that the disability in respect of whole body is required to be taken as 10%.

Thus, without disturbing the other parameters as assessed by the Tribunal i.e.,
Notional Income as Rs.14,000/-, multiplier to be applied is '18', the loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability comes to Rs.3,02,400/- (Rs.14,000/- X 12 X 18 X 10%).
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.2,11,680/- only under the said head.

Thus, the enhancement will be Rs.90,720/- (Rs.3,02,400/- - Rs.2,11,680/-).
NC: 2024:KHC:37447 7.
The amount awarded under the head pain and suffering i.e., Rs.20,000/- is grossly low as rightly contended by learned counsel for the appellant Sri.M.V.Maheshwarappa.

Having considered the nature of injury sustained and the treatment taken which includes surgery, this Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head pain and suffering.

Thus, the enhancement will be Rs.20,000/- (Rs.40,000/- - Rs.20,000/-).
8.

In the light of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the view that the appellant is thus entitled to a sum of Rs.1,10,720/- (Rs.90,720/- + Rs.20,000/-) in addition to the sum that is awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The compensation that is awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru through orders in MVC No.2728/2020 dated 10.03.2023 is enhanced by Rs.1,10,720/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
